source: Ferreira, Charest and Wimber (2019) Retrieval aids the creation of a generalised memory trace and strengthens episode-unique information. NeuroImage 201
finding: Gap 6 closed: the 2018 preprint (a05) was published in NeuroImage in 2019. Same design: scene-object pairs, retrieve vs restudy, two sessions two days apart, fMRI. mPFC activation rose across consecutive retrieval attempts. Category-level similarity rose. Episode-unique patterns were also strengthened. Both effects grew slowly across the two days, not within the session, and were strongest in parietal areas.
numbers: Europe PMC lists 35 citations. No test statistics read this session (abstract only).
quote: this strengthening does not come at the expense of episode-unique information
limits: Abstract only. The within-session hippocampal fall predicted by Antony 2017 is not claimed in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Retrieval can add a gist while keeping the specific detail. Argues against a rule that replaces detail with a summary.

source: Rowland (2014) The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: a meta-analytic review of the testing effect. Psychological Bulletin 140
finding: Abstract read again. Initial recall tests gave larger testing benefits than recognition tests. Support for effortful processing; limited support for the semantic elaboration account. Gap 5: the overall g is not in the abstract and the paper was not opened (paywalled; no open copy reached).
numbers: Overall g not obtained from a primary read. Europe PMC lists 358 citations. Secondary quotes of its related vs unrelated g: see d03.
agent_relevance: The agent's retrieval step should be recall-style (produce the answer), not recognition-style checking.

source: Gupta, Pan and Rickard (2026) Semantic relatedness and the efficacy of retrieval practice. npj Science of Learning 11:33
finding: Gap 5 partly closed. Quotes Rowland 2014: the cued-recall testing effect did not differ for related pairs (Hedges g = 0.66) vs unrelated pairs (g = 0.67), but that is a between-study contrast. Their own controlled experiment found the testing benefit about 26% smaller for highly related pairs than for weakly related pairs, 24 h later, not explained by ceiling.
numbers: N = 231 analysed (242 recruited; 118 low relatedness, 113 high). 80 English word pairs per list, one trial per pair. Restudy 6 s vs cued test with feedback (5 s plus 1 s feedback). Final cued recall after 24 h. Dual-memory reference model with cumulative distribution matching.
quote: its benefit was 26% smaller for highly related pairs
limits: One lab, one delay (24 h), word pairs only, university students. The ANOVA interaction was null and the authors call it uninterpretable; the model-based test found the reduction. 'Related' means word pairs, not schemas.
agent_relevance: Retrieval may help less where items are already strongly linked to what is known. For schema-rich notes the retrieve-first gain may be smaller; for isolated facts larger. This runs against a simple 'schema makes retrieval better' story.

source: Carpenter (2009) and Walsh and Rissman (2023), as described by Gupta et al. (2026)
finding: Secondary read. Carpenter 2009 Exp 1 found a smaller testing effect for high-relatedness pairs; Exp 2 found no relatedness effect. Walsh and Rissman 2023 (Nature Communications 14:7548) found no significant difference overall; a smaller effect only when restudy of all items was compared with test items answered correctly in training.
numbers: No numbers given in the passage read.
limits: Secondary description only; the two primary papers were not opened.
agent_relevance: Evidence that relatedness moderates the testing effect is mixed across three studies; treat as unsettled.

source: Tse et al. (2007) Schemas and memory consolidation. Science 316:76-82
finding: Gap 7 stays open. Abstract read: in rats, a paired-associate flavour-place task; memory became persistent as a schema gradually developed; one-trial new traces then became assimilated and rapidly hippocampus-independent; schemas played a causal role in lasting memory.
numbers: Europe PMC lists 918 citations. Days to schema, retention figures and lesion timing could not be read: the paper is not open and no open copy was reached.
limits: Abstract only. Rodent, one lab, flavour-place associations.
agent_relevance: The schema must be built first, over many trials, before new items integrate fast. A fresh agent store with no structure should not expect fast integration.

source: Testing the testing effect on Prolific: when retrieval practice fails to boost learning (2026), Experiment 1. Frontiers in Psychology
finding: A failed replication of the testing effect online. Undergraduates read two 500-word texts (expressionism, ancient Rome). In the test condition they answered 10 multiple-choice questions with feedback. Delayed test later. No condition effect.
numbers: N = 67 completed (169 recruited; 39.6% of the 120 eligible finished both phases). Total score /20: Expressionism control 8.68 (SD 5.19, n=38) vs test 8.88 (SD 2.84, n=29); Rome control 10.83 (SD 3.70, n=29) vs test 10.47 (SD 4.42, n=38). Condition F(1,66) = 0.13, p = 0.72; definition F = 0.94, p = 0.33; application F = 0.27, p = 0.61.
limits: Heavy attrition, online, small N, no power analysis or effect size reported. The text says one week in one place and ten weeks in another. Authors call it preliminary and not a direct replication.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: the benefit can vanish with weak engagement. An agent that skips the recall step and copies the note would be like a disengaged learner.

source: Testing the testing effect on Prolific (2026), Experiment 2. Frontiers in Psychology
finding: Second null result. Adults watched a 2 min 26 s lightning video with 19 key ideas, then wrote free recall (test) or rewatched; free recall two days later. No significant difference.
numbers: N = 129 completed (426 recruited; 30.3% finished). Ideas recalled of 19: control 6.51 (SD 5.74) vs test 7.44 (SD 4.65); Mann-Whitney U = 1773, p = 0.17, r = 0.14. Mean age 47.4.
limits: Small, noisy, online, high attrition. Direction was positive; r = 0.14 is small and the test is low powered. Not a refutation.
agent_relevance: The field effect (d about 0.5 overall) can fail to show in noisy samples; our agent test needs many items and several seeds.

source: Hippocampo-neocortical interaction as compressive retrieval-augmented generation (2026). Nature Communications
finding: Gap 9 partly informed. A model with a compressed episodic store and a neocortical generator (Mistral 7B fine-tuned on Wikipedia categories plus a story). Consolidation means training the generator on reconstructions. Recalled stories drift toward the training categories, like the Bartlett War of the Ghosts result in humans. Consolidating a compressed memory is called an approximation of an approximation.
numbers: 100 recalls sampled per topic, epoch 5, temperature 0.5. Drift measured as cosine distance of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings to the category mean. Human reference: Bergman and Roediger replication of Bartlett (distortions rise with delay). Exact distance values not read.
limits: A computational model, not an agent product test. Only the schema-distortion section was read. It trains weights; a note store is different.
agent_relevance: Consolidation by rewriting causes schema-driven distortion in an LLM. This is a mechanism for the hedge-to-fact and tense-flattening errors (b20, b21): keep the original next to the gist.

source: A complementary learning system for continual episodic memory in large language models (bioRxiv 2026)
finding: A fast hippocampus-like module gives each episode its own sparse low-rank adapter. Slow consolidation is batch replay fine-tuning of base weights. Streams of up to 1,000 factual and autobiographical episodes; each adapter needs only 2-3 parameters per token; recall stays high; after consolidation the model answers directly without adapters.
numbers: Up to 1,000 episodes. Accuracy figures not in the abstract.
limits: Preprint, abstract only, weight-level method. No retrieval-versus-restudy contrast.
agent_relevance: A weight-level analogue of fast store then slow consolidation. Not usable by a prompt-only scaffold; shows the two-speed design is being tried on LLMs.

source: An abstract relational map emerges in the human medial prefrontal cortex with consolidation (2026). Current Biology
finding: Side evidence for gap 6. fMRI repetition suppression and RSA show a relational (graph) representation in mPFC that emerged across two scanning sessions several days apart, not at once. Matches rodent work that abstraction takes days.
numbers: Europe PMC lists 6 citations. Sample and effect sizes not read.
limits: Abstract only. Not a retrieval-versus-restudy test, so it does not test Antony 2017 directly.
agent_relevance: Cortical abstraction is slow; a fast-consolidation claim for the agent should not promise same-session gains.

finding: No study found that tests an original-wording-kept fix. The problem papers (b20 LAPSE, b21 manufactured confidence) remain the only ones. d08 adds a mechanism: consolidation drifts toward the prior. d01 adds human support that retrieval can strengthen gist and detail together.
limits: Search limits: arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 on most calls and the WebSearch budget was used up, so this negative is weak. The d08 and d01 links are inference, not a measurement.
